note: He passes on profile and fails on the two criteria that decide whether a deal happens. Successful: runs his own company after 22 years of military service. Good to great: 27% body fat aiming at 10-12%, plateaued rather than in crisis, and he uses the phrase himself — 'taking it to the next level'. Not deconditioned: training six or seven times a week and walking 10,000 steps a day, the opposite of gym-averse, even though he is still well above his target weight. Income is a clear miss — 'I'm retired. I'm strapped for cash. I don't have six grand laying around', he does not make $150,000, he will not take on debt, and he priced the decision at $2,000 before hearing the number. The more interesting miss is neglected_health: the stated ICP assumes health is the area that has been let go, and for this prospect it is the area he is managing hardest. He has already produced a 68 lb loss unaided. There is no neglect to sell against, which is precisely why the cheaper-substitute objection is unanswerable here — the substitute is his own track record.
